WOODWORK — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: WOODWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Ignore burnt cables
   C. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

2. When learning Framed Wooden Doors and Windows, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.

3. When learning Design in Woodwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Design in Woodwork.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Design in Woodwork.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Design in Woodwork.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Design in Woodwork.

4. When learning Blending wood with other materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Blending wood with other materials.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Blending wood with other materials.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Blending wood with other materials.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Blending wood with other materials.

5. When learning Estimation of Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Estimation of Materials.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Estimation of Materials.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Estimation of Materials.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Estimation of Materials.

6. When learning Occupational Information, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Occupational Information.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Occupational Information.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Occupational Information.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Occupational Information.

7. When learning Fittings, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Fittings.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Fittings.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Fittings.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Fittings.

8. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

9. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Input Cable Tester
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. International Cricket Team

10. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Keyboard
   B. Monitor
   C. CPU
   D. Speaker

11. When learning Project Activity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project Activity.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project Activity.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Project Activity.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project Activity.

12. When learning Upholstery, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Upholstery.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Upholstery.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Upholstery.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Upholstery.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Blending wood with other materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Furniture Making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Framed Wooden Doors and Windows and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Fittings and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Never touch live wires with wet hands

2. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Framed Wooden Doors and Windows.

3. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Design in Woodwork.

4. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Blending wood with other materials.

5. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Estimation of Materials.

6. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Occupational Information.

7. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Fittings.

8. D — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

9. C — Information and Communication Technology

10. C — CPU

11. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project Activity.

12. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Upholstery.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Blending wood with other materials; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Furniture Making; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Framed Wooden Doors and Windows; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fittings; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
